topic: The Uncertainty Principle: The Fourier Trade-off

sections.title: Prerequisite Intuition: The Pulse and the Wave
lecture_lines: Signals exist in time and frequency domains.
The Fourier Transform decomposes complex signals.
A guitar pluck illustrates this duality perfectly.
animations: Fade in a pulse signal (#FF5733) at the origin.
Shift the pulse across the screen from left to right.
Introduce a sine wave (#33FF57) at the center.
Animate the pulse and sine wave overlapping.
Highlight the overlap area (#FFFF33) using a distinct color.

sections.title: The Duality Challenge
lecture_lines: Signals narrow in time broaden in frequency.
A brief pulse requires infinite frequencies.
This is the core duality challenge.
animations: Display a single point particle (#33A1FF) on screen.
Expand the point particle into a wave packet (#A133FF).
Show the trade-off by shrinking spatial width while frequency spreads.

sections.title: Mathematical Formulation (The Bound)
lecture_lines: Heisenberg-Gabor sets a fundamental bound.
Uncertainty is not a measurement error.
Wave packets obey this physical law.
Gaussian shapes minimize this uncertainty product.
Squeezing time forces frequency to widen.
animations: Fade in the Heisenberg inequality formula (#FFFFFF) centrally.
Highlight the spatial variance term (#FF3333) with a pulse.
Highlight the frequency variance term (#33FF33) with a pulse.
Show the product of the variances is greater than a constant (#FFFF33).
Draw a rectangle (#FF5733) representing the minimum uncertainty bound area.

sections.title: The Optimal Solution: Gabor Atoms
lecture_lines: The Gaussian is the optimal signal.
It acts as a perfect window.
Engineers use it to balance domains.
Detecting short chirps requires this precision.
It provides the ideal processing balance.
animations: Fade in the Gaussian function (#FF5733) as a central envelope.
Animate the Gaussian modulating a sine carrier wave (#33FF57).
Scale the Gaussian width to visualize the optimal uncertainty bound.
Overlay text indicating this is the optimal Gabor atom.
Flash the resulting Gabor atom to highlight its structural balance.

sections.title: Real-world Application: Modern Communication
lecture_lines: We cannot localize perfectly in both.
Resolution choice depends on specific goals.
Radar systems exemplify this critical trade-off.
Bats use pulses for different tasks.
Choosing resolution governs modern signal processing.
animations: Display a simulated radar communication spectrum plot (#33A1FF).
Overlay Gabor atoms (#A133FF) onto the noisy signal.
Show the reconstruction of original signals from these atoms (#33FF33).
